brief: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, 11 days after he resigned, after Trump lobbied over the weekend; the stock jumped as much as 34%, adding $1.1 trillion in market cap and halting Nasdaq futures. Nomura's McElligott reads the rescue as proof AI and equities are now too big to fail: the left-tail risk markets had been pricing is marked down, and that repricing mechanically forces buying through three channels. Phase 1: a vol crush deltas out dealers' short-gamma put hedges, forcing futures buybacks. Phase 2: a close above 7,043 flips the dominant signal window in Nomura's CTA trend-following model, forcing billions in futures purchases, though the model stays flat until 7,625. Vol-targeting funds must sell into the move, but Nomura projects roughly $41 billion of leveraged-ETF buying into the close, the second-largest on record, for about $60 billion of net forced buying overall before any discretionary investor acts. Goldman is positive on Huang's return for culture and the roadmap but flags unresolved DOJ/SEC probes and uncertainty over Nvidia's ecosystem financing scale, keeping its $220 target impaired. McElligott, JPMorgan and Deutsche Bank caution this is a positioning squeeze, not a resolution of tightening financial conditions or the Fed's hiking stance.

cards.anchor: it has historically taken six to eight weeks for volatility to subside and for stocks to bottom, with the S&P falling 14% to 16% on average outside of recessions

cards.document: Hedges Die, Shorts Get Stopped : McElligott Says AI Is Now Too Big To Fail As Jensen's Return Unleashes A $41BN Levered ETF Bid
cards.claim: Goldman's Ben Snider says an S&P bottom needs a catalyst restoring confidence in AI earnings, a better macro backdrop such as a dovish Fed signal, and a major washout in positioning.
cards.anchor: an S&P bottom needs three things: a catalyst that restores confidence in AI earnings, a better macro backdrop such as a dovish signal from the Fed, and a major washout in positioning

cards.document: Hedges Die, Shorts Get Stopped : McElligott Says AI Is Now Too Big To Fail As Jensen's Return Unleashes A $41BN Levered ETF Bid
cards.claim: The authors say the positioning washout for an S&P bottom is only half done: hedge funds have sold, but per Goldman's Lee Coppersmith, everyone else is still long.
cards.anchor: The positioning washout is half done. Hedge funds have puked, but as Goldman's Lee Coppersmith showed last night, everyone else is still long.

cards.document: Hedges Die, Shorts Get Stopped : McElligott Says AI Is Now Too Big To Fail As Jensen's Return Unleashes A $41BN Levered ETF Bid
cards.claim: The authors conclude the Trump put has a strike price around S&P 6,900 and Nvidia at 13 times Goldman's normalized earnings, while the Fed put still has none.
cards.anchor: The Trump put has a strike price, and it is somewhere around S&P 6,900 and Nvidia at 13 times Goldman's normalized earnings. The Fed put still doesn't have one.

cards.document: Hedges Die, Shorts Get Stopped : McElligott Says AI Is Now Too Big To Fail As Jensen's Return Unleashes A $41BN Levered ETF Bid
cards.claim: The authors say they lean toward the rally being a positioning squeeze inside a tightening cycle rather than the left tail being cut off for good.
cards.anchor: the left tail cut off for good, or a monster positioning squeeze inside a tightening cycle? We lean toward the second.
